title: Imran Khan asked to leave India: What rights do OCI cardholders have?
content: Actor Imran Khan faces deportation from India by October 28 due to his involvement in a protest. This action stems from a complaint lodged by BJP leader Kirit Somaiya regarding legal violations during the demonstration. Khan, a US citizen and OCI cardholder, was detained at the protest site in Mumbai. His participation raises questions about the rights of foreign nationals involved in political activities.

title: 'Will stand with Pak if US attacks': Rajasthan BJP chief’s remark sparks outcry
content: Rajasthan BJP president Madan Rathore stated that India would align with Pakistan in a potential US-Pakistan conflict. This statement has drawn significant criticism from Congress leaders, including Shama Mohamed. Mohamed questioned the BJP's stance and asked for clarification from Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Amit Shah. Rathore also accused Rahul Gandhi of inciting unrest and mentioned foreign interference in India's stability.

title: Ex-IAS Divya launches party: 10 civil servants who quit service to enter politics
content: Divya Mittal, an ex-IAS officer, has established the Jan Neeti Bharat party in preparation for the forthcoming elections. With a focus on enhancing citizen participation in policymaking rather than adhering to conventional governance methods, she aims to make a significant impact. Her decision to retire after 13 years in civil service aligns with a trend of bureaucrats entering politics.

title: Why New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani wants 15% of whatever NYU’s new quantum lab invents
content: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani has committed $29.2 million to NYU's Quantum Fabrication Facility (QFab) in Manhattan, set to open in 2030. In return, the city gets 15% of NYU's proceeds from intellectual property created with city-funded tools, plus three advisory board seats. Backed by $284 million in total funding, the new quantum lab will train CUNY students and support more than 100 companies.

title: California winery faces buyer deadline after $12.7m judgment and Chapter 11 case
content: California's 45-year-old Adelaida Vineyards faces an October 15 deadline to find a buyer after a family dispute led to a $12.7 million court judgment and bankruptcy filing. Court documents estimate its sale value at $3.8 million to $6.7 million, compared with $1.4 million to $2.8 million through liquidation. A proposed family settlement could prevent its closure.

title: US temple attack plot: Teen’s alleged manifesto describes Indians as ‘subhumans’
content: A 19-year-old white supremacist's intention to attack a temple near Chicago was disrupted by a rifle malfunction. Following the incident, concerned colleagues notified authorities after he expressed his intentions via messages. Police arrested Alexandros Paporakis, uncovering alarming materials including a manifesto that targeted several communities. The case has raised serious safety concerns among Hindu organizations about worship places.

title: Austin golf course could transfer to city after 50-year fight to protect it
content: Austin residents have passionately defended the historic Lions Municipal Golf Course for years, opposing potential developers. A new proposal seeks to officially hand over ownership of the golf course to the city, safeguarding its future. In return, the University of Texas would gain revised development regulations for neighboring properties on Lake Austin Boulevard. Officials assert that this arrangement effectively balances the need for green spaces with urban expansion.

title: Man allegedly posed as 49ers player to defraud 26 women of $1.3 million
content: Daejon Labrayae Love allegedly posed as a San Francisco 49ers player and used dating apps, luxury cars and fake investment accounts to target women in a $1.3 million fraud scheme. Prosecutors identified 26 victims, while the FBI is investigating claims from 35 additional potential victims. Love has pleaded not guilty to a federal conspiracy charge.

title: Michael Dell loses $20 billion in one day after Barclays downgrade
content: Michael Dell experienced a substantial decline in net worth, dropping more than $20 billion in just one day. This decline was prompted by a major decrease in his company's stock value following an analyst downgrade. Earlier this year, Dell's net worth had notably increased, bringing him closer to the highest billionaires in the world.

title: Oregon woman sold home to son-in-law for $270,000; court rejects right to stay
content: An Oregon woman who sold her home worth approximately $398,000 to her son-in-law for $270,000 in 2006 claimed she was promised the right to live there for life. After a dispute over her occupancy, a trial court ruled in her favour. However, the Oregon Court of Appeals overturned the decision, finding that the written sale documents transferred her entire ownership interest without reserving a life estate.

title: Justin Herbert’s $25,000 donation: How did it provide 100,000 meals to LA families?
content: Justin Herbert contributed $25,000 to the Los Angeles Regional Food Bank, which provided substantial meals during a tough holiday season. This donation was intended to help families facing food insecurity amidst ongoing pandemic challenges. Herbert emphasized the importance of community service, inspired by his parents' values. The Food Bank has been a crucial support system for families in need since 1973.

title: Mumbai shocker: CCTV clip shows 10-year-old pushing 18-month-old off 6th floor duct
content: Mumbai Police are investigating the death of an 18-month-old toddler, in Goregaon. She was reportedly thrown down from the sixth floor by a 10-year-old girl. The incident occurred while toddler was playing in the corridor of her housing society. After finding her injured, residents rushed her to a doctor, but she was declared dead.

title: 'Skipped dinner, wept': 'Blue drum' murder convicts' 1st night in jail

They were convicted for the brutal murder of Muskan's husband, Saurabh Rajput, earlier this year. The court described the murder as extremely cruel and grave, leading to their sentencing. Muskan is allowed to keep her infant daughter Radha with her while seeking permission to meet her elder daughter, Pihu.

title: No more guessing who's calling! Govt mandates caller ID display from Nov 1
content: The Department of Telecommunications is preparing to roll out Calling Name Presentation, a feature that shows the caller's name in addition to their number on the recipient's screen. This functionality will first be implemented on 4G networks before extending to other versions. Users will have the choice to opt-out if they utilize the calling line identification restriction service, striking a balance between enhancing caller recognition and safeguarding data privacy.

title: Andhra Pradesh shocker: Lover lured to pond, beaten to death; husband, wife arrested

Lakshmana allegedly had an extramarital affair with Lakshmi Durga, leading to disputes with her husband. Following a planned attack, he was murdered and his body dumped in a canal. Police arrested several individuals linked to the crime, including the couple, as the investigation progressed.

title: ‘Big items are done’: Envoy Gor hints major boost in India-US trade negotiations

Both sides have resolved major issues and are close to finalizing the agreement. Gor emphasized that the pace of negotiations is unusually swift compared to previous trade deals. External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar also indicated that progress ensures a positive outcome is imminent.

Overall, projections for India's merchandise exports remain optimistic as growth trends continue.

title: Stage 4 oral cancer survivor, 57, rebuilds strength and now deadlifts 80 kg

He paused his singing career to focus on her recovery, even crafting homemade gym equipment to aid in her rehabilitation. Remarkably, Javitri has progressed to deadlifting 80 kg, proving that with resilience and relentless effort, a rebirth of life is achievable for cancer patients.

Rescuers launched an intensive search, leading to her discovery on October 14, right before the onset of winter conditions. Although significantly weakened, Luna's return was met with joy and gratitude, both for her family and the devoted rescuers who never gave up on her.
